display.purpose: Headings, window title-bar captions, badge-scale chrome labels only — never body copy.

body.purpose: All read content: bio, descriptions, data readouts, nav labels.

motion.name: bevel-press
motion.purpose: Button hover/active bevel and translate steps — deliberately steppy, never eased smooth.

motion.name: rail-glide
motion.purpose: Commit-rail active indicator repositioning; plain CSS transition, not the View Transitions API (see DESIGN.md Do's and Don'ts).

motion.name: glitch-split
motion.purpose: One-frame RGB misregistration pulse on hover/focus, donated from the declined riso-misregistration challenger — deliberately kept red/cyan regardless of the theme accent.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The hero's 'RUN projects.exe' call to action.
components.css: .ds-pixel-btn { display: inline-block; font-family: 'Silkscreen', monospace; border: 2px solid #030a05; background: #142a19; color: #f2f6ee; padding: 12px 20px; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #f2f6ee, inset -2px -2px 0 #010601; transition: background 80ms steps(2), color 80ms steps(2); } .ds-pixel-btn:hover, .ds-pixel-btn:focus-visible { background: #f2f6ee; color: #06120a; }

components.name: Window
components.description: The system's signature container: a bordered, beveled OS window with a title bar, used for every content section.
components.css: .ds-window { border: 2px solid #030a05; background: #0d1f13; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #2d4a35, inset -1px -1px 0 #010601; } .ds-window-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; border-bottom: 2px solid #030a05; background: #030a05; padding: 8px 12px; } .ds-window-corner { width: 8px; height: 8px; background: #9caa9e; } .ds-window-corner--alt { background: #2a6b3f; } .ds-window-title { font-family: 'Silkscreen', monospace; font-size: 11px; color: #8fa392; } .ds-window-body { padding: 24px; color: #e9ecdf; font-family: 'VT323', monospace; font-size: 18px; }

components.name: Verdict Badge
components.description: Repo classification chip; color is always traceable to the repo's real GitHub topics.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-block; border: 1px solid; padding: 2px 8px; font-family: 'VT323', monospace; font-size: 14px; border-radius: 0; } .ds-badge--open { color: #5be07f; border-color: #2a6b3f; } .ds-badge--coursework { color: #ffbd4f; border-color: #7a5a1f; } .ds-badge--hackathon { color: #ff7ad1; border-color: #7a3562; } .ds-badge--research { color: #6f9dff; border-color: #2f4a7a; }

components.name: Commit Rail Node
components.description: One section node on the desktop-only left navigation rail, rendered as a git-graph.
components.css: .ds-rail-node { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 8px 0 8px 20px; text-decoration: none; } .ds-rail-dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; border: 1px solid #2d4a35; background: #030a05; } .ds-rail-node--active .ds-rail-dot { border-color: #f2f6ee; background: #f2f6ee; } .ds-rail-label { font-family: 'VT323', monospace; font-size: 18px; color: #6f8574; } .ds-rail-node--active .ds-rail-label { color: #f2f6ee; }

narrative.overview: The site does not decorate itself with pixel motifs — it renders as an actual 16-color computer that has just powered on. Every surface lives inside a bordered, beveled 'window' docked to a fixed region, the way a PC-98-era or early-Windows desktop composes itself from chrome, not cards. The system replaces the incumbent look entirely; that look is anti-reference only, kept nowhere in the new build. The environment is a blackish-green terminal housing — screen, grid, and chrome all live in that one dark hue — while a single white accent carries every link, button, and live number, so interactive content stands apart from the housing instead of blending into it. Two donated disciplines keep the world from reading as a costume: the site's own navigation is a literal git commit graph, and repo badges borrow judge-verdict coloring from competitive-programming scoreboards rather than an arbitrary tag palette. A third donation — a one-frame RGB channel misregistration pulse on hover/focus, lifted from risograph print misalignment — is the system's only 'glitch' and it never runs continuously.
keyCharacteristics: A blackish-green terminal housing (screen, grid, chrome) with a single white interactive accent — never a second green
Fixed 24px pixel grid as the page's literal material, kept low-contrast (~1.1:1 against the screen) so it reads as texture, not a bright foreground grid
Hard 2-tone bevel borders (inset/outset) stand in for all depth — no soft shadows anywhere
Two bitmap/CRT-lineage faces only: Silkscreen for display, VT323 for everything read at length
Live GitHub data rendered as terminal-style readouts, never restyled as generic stat cards
Repo preview images are ordered-dithered to the locked palette on canvas at load time

rules.name: The One-White Rule
rules.body: Exactly one bright, non-green accent exists (Terminal White) and it is reserved for interactive or live-data content. A second saturated color competing with it is a regression, not a variation.

rules.name: The Verdict Rule
rules.body: Color on a badge or status dot always means a classification a visitor could look up, never a mood or a decorative accent.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page is set in a third font. A word is either a computer's own label (Silkscreen) or content a person wrote (VT323).

rules.name: The No-Blur Rule
rules.body: Every depth cue is a hard 1px bevel pair. A soft or colored glow shadow never ships.

dos: Do keep every badge color traceable to the repo's actual GitHub topics/visibility.
Do dither any new photographic or screenshot imagery through the same ordered Bayer 4×4 pass at the locked duotone, with a plain-img fallback for CORS failures.
Do keep every text token at or above 4.5:1 contrast against its background.
Do keep the background grid subtle (near-1:1 contrast against the screen) — it is texture, not a foreground element.
donts: Don't call document.startViewTransition from a scroll-driven callback in this codebase — it reliably corrupted the page's paint near hydration in testing.
Don't introduce a soft or colored box-shadow anywhere.
Don't add a second saturated accent color alongside Terminal White outside the verdict badge system.
